Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats this as a latent ability or capacity to understand, parse, and execute natural-language instructions, and to keep outputs aligned with user intent, task goals, and explicit constraints. Most definitions make constraint satisfaction central, often naming format, style, word limits, JSON validity, requested languages, or multi-step procedures, and several extend the same basic idea to multimodal, multilingual, retrieval, agent, and embodied settings. A smaller line of work defines it more behaviorally, as the observable act of producing a compliant response or action, and a few papers narrow it further to exact-specification matching, system-message compliance over turns, or evaluator-side judgment of whether a response satisfies an instruction.

Space of facets. Papers most often organize the concept by what must be followed: guidelines, constraints, rules, system messages, or broader open-ended instructions. Several narrower labels tighten the focus to exact specification matching or condition satisfaction, while one evaluation-oriented line breaks instruction-following into relevance, factuality, and adherence, and system-message work separates constraint violation, instruction misjudgement, and multi-turn instability. The naming is only partly stable: many labels look like setting-specific variants of the same core ability, but a few usages shift meaning more substantially, such as treating rule-following as a disposition toward order and norms rather than prompt-conditioned task execution.

Space of measurement. Operationalization is wide: papers link the construct to 27 measurement instruments and 10 behavioral indicators. The most common instruments are MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2.0, IFEval, Arena-Hard, and AlpacaEval, mostly benchmark suites for conversational or general instruction following; the remaining instruments include other benchmarks, LLM-as-a-judge procedures, and human evaluation. At the response level, papers often check concrete behaviors such as staying within a word limit, emitting valid JSON, answering in the requested format or language, following system-message constraints across turns, or satisfying multiple constraints in one prompt, so the measures usually match the adherence side of the definitions even when the definitions are broader than benchmarked response quality or verifiable compliance.

Links. Several papers claim causal relationships from instruction-following ability to chain of thought and tool use, and to several downstream outcomes. A smaller line also claims causal relationships from other capabilities back to instruction-following ability. It is reported to correlate with reasoning, with one paper describing a negative correlation between instruction-following ability and model scale in reasoning tasks, and papers further describe it as related to several other properties and tasks.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage treats this as a latent ability or capacity to understand, parse, and execute natural-language instructions, and to keep outputs aligned with user intent, task goals, and explicit constraints. Most definitions make constraint satisfaction central, often naming format, style, word limits, JSON validity, requested languages, or multi-step procedures, and several extend the same basic idea to multimodal, multilingual, retrieval, agent, and embodied settings. A smaller line of work defines it more behaviorally, as the observable act of producing a compliant response or action, and a few papers narrow it further to exact-specification matching, system-message compliance over turns, or evaluator-side judgment of whether a response satisfies an instruction.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Papers most often organize the concept by what must be followed: guidelines, constraints, rules, system messages, or broader open-ended instructions. Several narrower labels tighten the focus to exact specification matching or condition satisfaction, while one evaluation-oriented line breaks instruction-following into relevance, factuality, and adherence, and system-message work separates constraint violation, instruction misjudgement, and multi-turn instability. The naming is only partly stable: many labels look like setting-specific variants of the same core ability, but a few usages shift meaning more substantially, such as treating rule-following as a disposition toward order and norms rather than prompt-conditioned task execution.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Operationalization is wide: papers link the construct to 27 measurement instruments and 10 behavioral indicators. The most common instruments are MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2.0, IFEval, Arena-Hard, and AlpacaEval, mostly benchmark suites for conversational or general instruction following; the remaining instruments include other benchmarks, LLM-as-a-judge procedures, and human evaluation. At the response level, papers often check concrete behaviors such as staying within a word limit, emitting valid JSON, answering in the requested format or language, following system-message constraints across turns, or satisfying multiple constraints in one prompt, so the measures usually match the adherence side of the definitions even when the definitions are broader than benchmarked response quality or verifiable compliance.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: Several papers claim causal relationships from instruction-following ability to chain of thought and tool use, and to several downstream outcomes. A smaller line also claims causal relationships from other capabilities back to instruction-following ability. It is reported to correlate with reasoning, with one paper describing a negative correlation between instruction-following ability and model scale in reasoning tasks, and papers further describe it as related to several other properties and tasks.

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define instruction following ability as a model's ability or tendency to understand, interpret, and comply with natural language instructions or prompt-specified constraints in order to execute the requested task or produce the requested output. Differences are mainly about setting, modality, complexity, or emphasis on formatting and constraints, while only a few outliers apply the term to narrower cases like evaluators, retrievers, embedders, or broader norm-following dispositions.
